title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.30 fixes the dead code family where it could break a build or a running app: a Delete quick fix that landed on the wrong lines after an unsaved edit, a manifest activity reported as missing on a large project and offered for removal, a custom view constructor whose `attrs` parameter looked unused, a shrinker keep list reported as an unused resource, and Room enums whose entries come back from the database.

highlights.title: The fix deletes the right lines
highlights.description: Removal extents are recomputed on the current text, so an unsaved edit above a declaration no longer shifts the deletion, and annotations spanning several lines go with their declaration.

highlights.title: Nothing removed on a guess
highlights.description: A capped file listing no longer reports a live activity as missing, a custom view keeps its inflation constructor, and a shrinker keep list keeps the resources it protects.

highlights.title: Runtime readers respected
highlights.description: Room enums, strings reached by getIdentifier, Kotlin test classes outside a Gradle test source set and modules published through a version catalog are no longer reported as dead.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Quick fixes recompute their extent on the current text, and the shared corpus refreshes as soon as an open editor differs from the scan.
A multiline annotation, an annotation holding a keyword in its argument, and a qualified `@Subscribe` are removed with their declaration.
Past the source file cap, no manifest component and no dependency is offered for removal.
`attrs: AttributeSet?`, `res/raw/keep.xml` and the resources its wildcards protect, and strings reached by `getIdentifier` stay put.
Room `@Entity` enums, Kotlin `@Test` classes in any folder, and modules published through a catalog alias are no longer reported as dead.
